newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour divides architectural spoils of victory.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour divides architectural spoils of victory.

text.p: The leaders of Britain's "Peoples' Party" can live like aristocrats now they have won power.

The spoils of election victory for Tony Blair's Labour Party include a collection of historic London mansions and huge country houses, complete with servants and vast gardens, which go with the top jobs in government.
Labour's top politicians, fresh from a landslide win over the Conservatives last Thursday which ended 18 years in opposition, are taking their pick.
Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott, a former waiter on an ocean liner, has chosen the spectacular London building which used to be the headquarters of Britain's naval chiefs.

But it was the convenience of living close to parliament, rather than the wood-panelled rooms, full-sized painting of Admiral Horatio Nelson and views of Buckingham Palace and Trafalgar Square that made him choose Admiralty House as his new home, Prescott explained.
"I have had an opportunity to live closer to government," he told BBC television. "I've taken that, of course."
Robin Cook, another leading representative of the left in the new cabinet, wins country weekends at Chevening as a perk of his new job as foreign secretary.

Chevening is a 17th-century, 115-room mansion in the Kent countryside, with 3,500 acres (1,400 hectares) of gardens and corridors lined with Huguenot tapestries donated by the King of Prussia in 1708.
Cook will be following in the footsteps of Prince Charles, heir to the throne, who lived in Chevening for six years.

In case the mansion is not enough, Cook also gets 1 Carlton Terrace, a stately London house overlooking St James's Park where France's Napoleon III once lived in exile. The government revealed in 1994 that the London house cost taxpayers more than 320,000 pounds ($520,000) a year in rent and upkeep.

Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown also gets a mansion as part of his job package: Dorneywood in Buckinghamshire, which boasts six bedrooms, 14 reception rooms, 214 acres (85 hectares) of gardens and a full complement of servants.
It was not clear, however, whether Brown would use the building -- he reportedly told colleagues in February that he would rather the house was opened to the public.
Former chancellor Norman Lamont had no such qualms about making the most of Dorneywood.

"I have never forgotten the face of Henry, the butler, when we first met," Lamont wrote in the Daily Telegraph. "He asked me how often I would be coming to Dorneywood. When I told him we would be coming every weekend, he was quite disconcerted."
Prime Minister Blair gets Chequers, a 400-year-old country mansion. Blair would also traditionally get 10 Downing Street, the famous London prime-ministerial residence.
But Blair decided Number 10 would be too cramped to accommodate his wife and three children, as it has only four bedrooms, two bathrooms and a small kitchen and dining room.
He has chosen instead to live in Number 11 next door, traditionally the London residence of the chancellor, which has five bedrooms, seven bathrooms and spacious reception rooms.
Brown, who is single, will live in Number 10. ($1=.6208 Pound)
